Today, they are more likely to contain:
🍟 Chips

The good news is that small changes can make a meaningful difference.

The goal is not perfection. It is helping children develop a healthier relationship with food through simple, mindful swaps made one step at a time. 💜

1. Ajwain Sek

"GRISHMA RUTUCHARYA: Summer Routine"

Ayurveda explains that summer heat reduces body fluids, increases Vata, and weakens overall energy. That’s why your diet and lifestyle should change with the season.

Summer Ayurveda Tips:
• Eat light, cooling & easy-to-digest foods
• Stay hydrated naturally
• Include seasonal fruits & fresh drinks
• Prefer sweet (madhura) potency foods

👍 Best Summer Foods: Watermelon, coconut water, fresh buttermilk, ghee, moong, rice, dudhi, pumpkin & seasonal fruits.

🧉 Natural Cooling Drinks: Aam panna, rose water, vetiver water, fennel-coriander water, lemon water, sattu drink & gulkand water.

❌ Avoid: Spicy, oily, fermented, stale & excessively hot foods, alcohol, smoking & excessive sun exposure.

🌿 Lifestyle Matters Too: Wear light cotton clothes, avoid direct heat, stay calm, hydrated, & avoid overexertion.

"Balance your summer naturally with Ayurveda."

Ayurveda has always carried timeless wisdom.

What changes is simply the way each generation communicates it.

This carousel brings together two perspectives. The structured clarity of traditional Ayurvedic understanding and the relatable language of modern digital culture.

From doshas and daily routines to Panchakarma and root-cause healing, the essence remains the same: BALANCE, AWARENESS, HOLISTIC WELL-BEING.

Because ancient knowledge can still feel relevant, accessible, and deeply understood in today’s world.

Which side are you on, Millennial PR Team or Gen Z Social Team?

Summer wellness is about choosing drinks that truly cool and nourish the body from within.

From buttermilk and bael juice to tender coconut, munakka water & kokum sharbat.
Ayurveda has long recommended these traditional summer super drinks to support hydration, digestion, energy, and internal balance during hot weather.

Why they matter:
• Help prevent dehydration
• Support natural body cooling
• Aid digestion & gut health
• Reduce fatigue & summer exhaustion

Simple seasonal choices can make a powerful difference to your overall well-being.

REALITY: It only creates a temporary cooling sensation.

According to Ayurveda, excessive consumption of cold foods can weaken digestion, increase heaviness, and disrupt the body’s natural balance.

True cooling comes from supporting the body internally, not just creating a surface-level sensation.

While watermelon is naturally refreshing and hydrating, Ayurveda explains that consuming it the wrong way can affect digestion, weaken agni, and disturb dosha balance.

In this feature, Dr. Priyanka Rajyagor breaks down the right time, quantity, and combinations for eating watermelon to truly benefit your health and well-being.

Because in Ayurveda, it’s not just about what you eat, it’s about how and when you eat it.
